While the statement underscores pandemic-related downside risks, its policy stance reflects a supportive, literature-consistent framework. With inflation below 2% and a sizable output gap, maintaining the funds rate at 0–0.25% and conducting large-scale Treasury and agency MBS purchases aligns with Taylor-rule guidance and inflation-forecast/average-inflation targeting approaches (Clarida–Galí–Gertler; Svensson and Woodford; Bernanke et al.). The willingness to let inflation run moderately above 2% to achieve an average target is designed to anchor expectations near 2%, while asset purchases work through credit and term-premium channels to support market functioning and lending (Bernanke–Gertler; term-structure evidence such as Piazzesi/Rudebusch). Net tone: cautious on near-term outlook but materially supportive on policy, implying a less negative sentiment than a purely risk-focused reading.
